result.markdown: --- title: "Session 3 — Propensity Scores and Matching" subtitle: "Propensity score · overlap · matching · balance · love plot · effect in the matched sample · Lab 3" author: "Community Medicine Workshop" format: revealjs: theme: serif css: [../assets/slide_deck.css, assets/workshop.css, assets/quiz.css] include-after-body: assets/quiz-include.html embed-resources: true slide-number: true navigation-mode: linear code-copy: true center: false transition: fade width: 1280 height: 720 fig-align: center html-math-method: plain execute: echo: true warning: false message: false fig-width: 9 fig-height: 4.6 fig-dpi: 100 --- ## Where we are ::: {.incremental} - Session 2: adjust in the **outcome model** - Today: model the **treatment assignment** instead, and build **comparable groups** before looking at the outcome - By the end you can: - estimate a **propensity score** and check **overlap** - **match** and check **balance** - estimate the effect in the matched sample ::: # Topic 1 — The propensity score {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Probability of enrolment ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ps_model <- glm(f_ps, data = htn, family = binomial) htn$ps <- predict(ps_model, type = "response") htn |> group_by(programme) |> summarise(min = round(min(ps), 2), mean = round(mean(ps), 2), max = round(max(ps), 2)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 2 × 4 programme min mean max 1 0 0.04 0.35 0.87 2 1 0.07 0.49 0.97 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - **Propensity score** = P(enrolled | confounders). Two adults with the **same score** have, on average, the **same confounder distribution**: like a small randomised trial - Include the **confounders** (and predictors of the outcome); **not** mediators, colliders or variables that only predict enrolment - The aim is **balance**, not prediction: do **not** judge it by the AUC ::: ## Overlap (positivity) ::: {.cell output-location='slide'} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(htn, aes(ps, fill = factor(programme, labels = c("Not enrolled", "Enrolled")))) + geom_density(alpha = 0.5) + scale_fill_manual(values = c(col_blue, col_red)) + labs(x = "Propensity score", fill = NULL) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](s3_propensity_matching_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-3-1.png){width=900} ::: ::: ::: {.key} The two distributions **overlap** over almost the whole range: for nearly every enrolled adult there are **comparable** non-enrolled adults. Regions **without** overlap cannot be compared without **extrapolation**. ::: # Topic 2 — Matching {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Balance before matching ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} bal.tab(f_ps, data = htn, un = TRUE, s.d.denom = "pooled")$Balance[, "Diff.Un", drop = FALSE] |> round(2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Diff.Un age 0.43 sex_Male 0.00 education_None -0.08 education_Primary -0.04 education_Secondary+ 0.11 urban 0.12 bmi 0.11 diabetes 0.12 baseline_sbp 0.63 ``` ::: ::: **Standardised mean difference (SMD)**: difference in means divided by the SD. **Below 0.1** is the usual target. Here **baseline SBP 0.63** and **age 0.43**: far off. ## 1:1 nearest-neighbour matching ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} m_out <- matchit(f_ps, data = htn, method = "nearest", distance = "glm", caliper = 0.2) m_out ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` A `matchit` object - method: 1:1 nearest neighbor matching without replacement - distance: Propensity score [matching, caliper] - estimated with logistic regression - caliper: (0.037) - number of obs.: 3000 (original), 2114 (matched) - target estimand: ATT - covariates: age, sex, education, urban, bmi, diabetes, baseline_sbp ``` ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - Each enrolled adult is paired with the **non-enrolled adult with the closest score**; the **caliper** (0.2 SD) refuses poor matches - **2,114 adults (1,057 pairs)** remain; **172 enrolled** adults found no match - No outcome data are used: the design is fixed **before** looking at SBP ::: ## Balance after matching ::: {.cell output-location='slide'} ```{.r .cell-code} love.plot(m_out, thresholds = 0.1, abs = TRUE, stars = "raw") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](s3_propensity_matching_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-6-1.png){width=900} ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} bal.tab(m_out, un = TRUE)$Balance[c("age", "diabetes", "baseline_sbp"), c("Diff.Un", "Diff.Adj")] |> round(2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Diff.Un Diff.Adj age 0.42 0.05 diabetes 0.12 0.01 baseline_sbp 0.63 0.06 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.key} All SMDs are now **below 0.1** (baseline SBP 0.63 → 0.06). Judge matching by **balance**, never by p-values. If balance is poor, **change the propensity model** (add interactions, curves) and match again. ::: # Topic 3 — The effect {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## In the matched sample ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} md <- match.data(m_out) fit_m <- lm(sbp_12m ~ programme, data = md, weights = weights) round(coeftest(fit_m, vcov. = vcovCL, cluster = ~subclass)["programme", 1:2], 2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Estimate Std. Error -5.94 0.51 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - **−5.9 mmHg** (SE 0.51): close to the regression estimate - SE **clustered on the matched pair** - Matching the enrolled targets the **ATT**, here for the **enrolled who could be matched**: say so, and describe who was **dropped** - Adding the covariates to this model ("double adjustment") removes residual imbalance ::: ## Strengths and limits | Strength | Limit | |---|---| | Separates **design** from **outcome analysis** | Only **measured** confounders are balanced | | **Balance** is visible and checkable | Discards unmatched people (precision, target population) | | Easy to explain | Many choices (caliper, ratio, replacement): **pre-specify** | ## 🔧 Switch to R — Lab 3 {.lab-slide background-color="#1565c0"} ::: {.lab-box} **File:** `causal-workshop/labs/lab3_match.R` - propensity score and overlap plot - matching with a caliper, balance table and love plot - effect in the matched data ::: **Time:** 40 minutes · answer the Q questions in the comments ## Self-check quiz (1/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="z3q1" data-type="mcq" data-hash="b4fe0y.4csr1p" data-show="VGhlIHByb2JhYmlsaXR5IG9mIHJlY2VpdmluZyB0aGUgZXhwb3N1cmUsIGdpdmVuIHRoZSBt ZWFzdXJlZCBjb25mb3VuZGVycw==" data-explain="VGhlIHByb3BlbnNpdHkgc2NvcmUgc3VtbWFyaXNlcyB0aGUgbWVhc3VyZWQgY29uZm91bmRl cnMgaW50byBvbmUgbnVtYmVyOiB0aGUgY2hhbmNlIG9mIGJlaW5nIGV4cG9zZWQuIEFkdWx0 cyB3aXRoIHRoZSBzYW1lIHNjb3JlIGFyZSBjb21wYXJhYmxlIG9uIHRob3NlIGNvbmZvdW5k ZXJzLg=="} What is a propensity score? - The probability of the outcome, given the exposure and the measured confounders - The number of confounders on which two adults in the data agree exactly - The share of the outcome variance that the exposure explains in the model - The probability of receiving the exposure, given the measured confounders ::: ## Self-check quiz (2/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="z3q2" data-type="mcq" data-hash="b4fr9k.4ct5iz" data-show="QnkgY292YXJpYXRlIGJhbGFuY2UsIGUuZy4gc3RhbmRhcmRpc2VkIGRpZmZlcmVuY2VzIGJl bG93IDAuMQ==" data-explain="VGhlIHB1cnBvc2Ugb2YgdGhlIHNjb3JlIGlzIHRvIGJhbGFuY2UgY29uZm91bmRlcnMgYmV0 d2VlbiBncm91cHMuIEEgaGlnaCBBVUMgY2FuIGV2ZW4gc2lnbmFsIHBvb3Igb3ZlcmxhcC4="} How should you judge whether propensity-score matching has worked? - By covariate balance, e.g. standardised differences below 0.1 - By the AUC of the propensity model, which should be above 0.8 - By the p-value of the exposure in the matched outcome model - By the number of adults that are kept in the matched sample ::: ## Self-check quiz (3/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="z3q3" data-type="mcq" data-hash="b4g4ia.4ctk0d" data-show="U29tZSBhZHVsdHMgaGF2ZSBubyBjb21wYXJhYmxlIGNvdW50ZXJwYXJ0LCBzbyB0aGVpciBl ZmZlY3QgaXMgbm90IGVzdGltYWJsZQ==" data-explain="V2l0aG91dCBvdmVybGFwIChwb3NpdGl2aXR5KSB0aGUgY29tcGFyaXNvbiByZWxpZXMgb24g ZXh0cmFwb2xhdGlvbi4gVGhlIGhvbmVzdCBvcHRpb25zIGFyZSB0byByZXN0cmljdCB0aGUg cG9wdWxhdGlvbiBvciB0byBhY2NlcHQgdGhhdCB0aGUgZWZmZWN0IGlzIG5vdCBpZGVudGlm aWVkIHRoZXJlLg=="} The propensity distributions of the two groups hardly overlap. What does this mean? - The propensity model is correct, as it discriminates well between the two groups - Some adults have no comparable counterpart, so their effect is not estimable - The exposure has a strong effect on the outcome in most adults of the cohort - Matching will work especially well, because the two groups are so distinct ::: ## Self-check quiz (4/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="z3q4" data-type="mcq" data-hash="b4ghr1.4ctyhs" data-show="VGhlIGVzdGltYXRlIGFwcGxpZXMgdG8gdGhlIG1hdGNoZWQgZW5yb2xsZWQgYWR1bHRzLCBh IGNoYW5nZWQgdGFyZ2V0" data-explain="RHJvcHBpbmcgdW5tYXRjaGVkIGFkdWx0cyBwcm90ZWN0cyBjb21wYXJhYmlsaXR5IGJ1dCBj aGFuZ2VzIHdobyB0aGUgcmVzdWx0IGlzIGFib3V0LiBSZXBvcnQgaG93IG1hbnkgd2VyZSBk cm9wcGVkIGFuZCB3aG8gdGhleSB3ZXJlLg=="} In 1:1 matching, 172 enrolled adults found no match within the caliper. What is the consequence? - The estimate is biased by the caliper, which should therefore be removed - The 172 adults should be matched to the nearest adult, whatever the distance - Nothing follows, since dropped adults do not affect a matched analysis - The estimate applies to the matched enrolled adults, a changed target ::: ## Self-check quiz (5/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="z3q5" data-type="mcq" data-hash="b4guzn.4cucz2" data-show="Q29uZm91bmRlcnMgbWVhc3VyZWQgYmVmb3JlIHRoZSBleHBvc3VyZSwgY2hvc2VuIGZyb20g dGhlIERBRw==" data-explain="VGhlIHNjb3JlIG11c3QgYmFsYW5jZSBwcmUtZXhwb3N1cmUgY29uZm91bmRlcnMuIFBvc3Qt ZXhwb3N1cmUgdmFyaWFibGVzIChtZWRpYXRvcnMsIGNvbGxpZGVycykgYmlhcyB0aGUgZXN0 aW1hdGUsIGhvd2V2ZXIgd2VsbCB0aGV5IHByZWRpY3Qu"} Which variables belong in the propensity-score model? - Confounders measured before the exposure, chosen from the DAG - Mediators such as adherence, since they predict the outcome well - Colliders such as clinic visits, since they predict enrolment well - All the available variables, selected by a stepwise procedure ::: ## Score and take-home **Your score: ** ::: {.incremental} - **Propensity score** = P(exposure | confounders) - Check **overlap** (positivity) first - **Match**, then check **balance** (SMD < 0.1, love plot) - Estimate in the matched data with **pair-clustered SE** - Matching targets the **ATT** and balances only **measured** confounders ::: **Next:** Session 4: inverse probability weighting

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
